content: I'll start by reading the test image and the part index file simultaneously.

The test image shows a **stem** with a lesion/canker at a node junction — the stem appears tan/brown, collapsed/girdled at the affected area, with some white cottony-looking growth on the necrotic tissue and wilted leaves hanging below.

From the part index, the stem candidates are: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Anthracnose, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Bacterial_Wilt, Early_Blight, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Phytophthora_Blight, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt.

The white cottony growth on the stem + girdling at a node strongly suggests Sclerotinia or Gray_Mold. Let me view reference images for my top candidates.
Sclerotinia shows black sclerotia and white mycelium — somewhat similar. Now let me check Gray_Mold.

The bottom-right panel of Gray_Mold shows a stem lesion at a node that matches the test image very closely — tan/brown necrotic tissue at the node with some grayish mycelium. Let me check two more candidates.

Southern_Blight shows lesions typically at the soil line with fan-shaped white mycelium — less consistent with the mid-plant node location in the test image.

**Summary of analysis:**
- **Test image**: Stem lesion at a branch node junction, tan/brown necrotic girdling, white/grayish cottony mycelium on lesion surface, wilted tissue below
- **Gray_Mold** reference (bottom-right panel): Near-identical stem canker at a node with tan-brown necrotic tissue and grayish mycelium — best match
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Shows black sclerotia and white mycelium, but lesions tend to be on lower stems/near soil; sclerotia not visible in test image
- **Southern_Blight**: Typically at soil line with radiating white mycelial fans — location doesn't match

The stem node canker with grayish-white cottony mycelium and collapse is the hallmark of Botrytis (Gray_Mold).
